s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral, affecting the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation are present in the affected skin
Motion of the right limb joint is slightly limited
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings include normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral, affecting the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation are present in the affected skin
Motion of the right limb joint is slightly limited
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings include normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

raw.rationale: The patient's unilateral skin hardening, mild hypertrichosis, and hyperpigmentation, along with the MRI and histopathological findings, are consistent with Linear Scleroderma, which typically presents with progressive, asymmetric skin hardening and limited joint mobility.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea typically presents with well-defined, circular or oval patches of skin hardening, which is not consistent with the patient's ill-defined, stony-hard plaque.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma is a systemic disease that typically affects multiple areas of the body and is associated with autoantibodies, which were not present in this patient.

rejected.label: Stiff Skin Syndrome
rejected.why: Stiff Skin Syndrome is a rare disease characterized by diffuse, rock-hard skin induration, which is not consistent with the patient's localized skin hardening.

rejected.label: Fibroblastic Rheumatism
rejected.why: Fibroblastic Rheumatism is a rare disease characterized by joint contractures and skin thickening, but it typically presents with more pronounced joint involvement and systemic symptoms, which are not present in this patient.
